Assess Solar Trackers for Suitable Project Sites

Thematic Area: Solar Tracking & System Performance

How might we identify sites where solar tracking can improve lifetime project value after accounting for installation, operating and maintenance requirements?

Background

An Indonesian solar EPC business has named solar tracker systems among the technologies it wants to explore to strengthen the value of its solar solutions.

The objective is to identify sites where moving panels to follow the sun improves lifetime project value. Relevant partners provide tracker hardware, control systems, design support and performance modelling.

Tracker design should reflect available space, mounting requirements, shading, wind conditions and maintenance access. The collaboration will compare tracking with fixed-tilt systems for suitable project sites.

Significance of Problem

Without an effective solution, the challenges include:

  • Missed applications: A clear comparison with fixed systems helps identify projects where tracking offers additional value.
  • Difficult investment decisions: Added equipment and maintenance costs need a credible lifetime financial assessment.
  • Integration challenges: Poor alignment with site and engineering requirements creates layout, structural and operating difficulties.

Existing Efforts

  • Technology priority: Solar trackers form part of the business’s requested technology capabilities.
  • Partner roles: Combine monitoring and project-support information with specialist tracker hardware and engineering expertise to develop the tracking system.
  • Collaboration focus: Select a suitable site and compare fixed-tilt and tracking alternatives using consistent assumptions. Review generation, capital cost, shading, controls, wind conditions, maintenance access and local support. Use engineering-approved designs and measure operation and output in the trial.

Potential Market Size

  • Global tracker demand: Global solar-tracker equipment shipments exceeded 134 GWdc in 2025, increasing 19% from 2024. European shipments reached 25 GWdc.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
